title: Multi-modal Consumption Acceleration Playbook
author: Maya Qureshi
body:
Summary

This playbook describes the product, commercial, and operational plan to accelerate customer adoption of multi-modal consumption on Redwood Inference (image + text + audio). It combines a short product overview, PRD-level requirements, a design-spec summary for the runtime and client UX, pricing and packaging options for trials and scale, a roadmap with milestones, and a release/launch checklist. Target audience: product managers, solutions engineering, pricing, go-to-market, platform engineering, and customer success.

Goals and success metrics

- Primary goal: Enable customers to add multi-modal features (image understanding, multimodal chat, and audio transcription/LLM fusion) with clear cost predictability and minimal integration work.
- Adoption KPIs (90-day window post-launch):
  1. 25% of new enterprise trials include at least one multi-modal route.
  2. 10 production customers with >1M multi-modal tokens (or equivalent units) per month within first 6 months.
  3. 30% reduction in trial-to-paid time for customers adopting multi-modal features compared to baseline.
- Operational KPIs: average 95th percentile latency increase <= 15% vs. text-only baseline; error rate for multi-modal routes < 0.5% P95; cost per multimodal request bounded by pricing bands below.

Product overview / value proposition

- What: A coherent consumption surface and runtime guarantees that let developers call combined text + image/audio endpoints, get unified response streaming and token accounting, and choose fidelity tiers for model variants.
- Who: Developers building search, document understanding, visual QA, voice assistants, and content extraction workflows for cloud-native SaaS and regulated enterprises.
- Why now: Rapid customer requests for combined modalities, and competitive differentiator for those who need predictable economics and production SLOs across modalities.

High-level requirements (PRD bullets)

1. Unified API surface
   - Endpoint: POST /v1/multi/generate with payload supporting text prompts, base64 image list or image URLs, and optional audio blob references.
   - Response: Streaming chunked responses with metadata segments indicating modality origin (text/image/audio) and token accounting.
   - Backwards compatibility: fall back to existing text-only endpoints via flag `text_only: true`.
2. Consumption model and telemetry
   - Metering unit: define a single canonical "consumption unit" (CU) that maps to token-equivalents across modalities. Document mapping and rounding.
   - Telemetry events: multimodal.request.start, multimodal.segment.processed, multimodal.kv_cache.hit/miss, multimodal.fallback.triggered.
3. Runtime SLOs and fallbacks
   - Latency SLOs: P95 end-to-end generation latency <= 800ms for single-image short prompts (<=256 tokens).
   - Fallbacks: model variant fallback path if image encoder unavailable or quantized variant fails; automatic degrade to text-only summary when image parsing fails and `fallback_policy: degrade_to_text` is enabled.
4. Security and data handling
   - Encrypted at-rest for transient artifacts, ephemeral cache TTL <= 24 hours by default for image blobs; opt-in retention for enterprise customers only.
5. Developer ergonomics
   - SDK updates for Node/Python/Go with typed request builders and local validation for common misconfigurations (image size, unsupported format).
   - Quickstart templates for visual Q&A, document ingestion with OCR + LLM fusion, and voice-to-summary workflows.

Design-spec highlights (runtime + UX)

A. Runtime: hybrid preprocessor + fusion model routing
- Inference pipeline stages: blob ingestion -> modality encoders (image/audio) -> fusion request composer -> model selector -> generation -> post-processing.
- Kernel and batching: continuous batching for fusion requests with adaptive micro-batching windows; preferential scheduling for low-latency single-image requests.
- KV cache coordination: separate cache namespaces per modality with coordinated eviction to avoid cross-modality pollution. Cache TTL policies exposed in config API.

B. API and UX decisions
- Schema: unified request JSON allows array of "inputs" with {type: text|image|audio, data: ...}; responses include labelled segments and confidence scores.
- Streaming: multi-part SSE streams where each event has modality tag, token range, and cost delta so clients can show partial multimodal content progressively.

C. Fallbacks and compatibility matrix
- If image encoder times out, route to text-only variant and emit multimodal.fallback.triggered with reason.
- Compatibility table (excerpt):
| Feature | Hosted | Dedicated | Private (VPC) | Notes |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| Image upload via URL | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | URL fetcher available only in hosted by default (configurable for private) |
| Audio streaming | ✓ | ✓ | restricted | Websocket required for low-latency bi-directional streams |
| On-prem image preprocessor | ✗ (managed) | ✓ | ✓ | Private customers may supply their own preprocessor binary |

Pricing & packaging options (recommended)

- Objectives: reduce friction for experimentation while protecting unit economics for high-throughput customers.
- Offer tiers:
  1. Trial (free credits) — bundled 1000 multimodal CUs for 30 days; restricted to hosted.
  2. Developer (pay-as-you-go) — per-CU price with sliding discount after 1M CU/month.
  3. Dedicated (reserved) — capacity-based commitment with discounted CU rate and optional private preprocessors.
  4. Enterprise bundle — custom SLA, retention options, and per-route fidelity crediting.
- Pricing heuristics: map large images and long audio to higher CU weights; provide a cost estimator SDK function `estimate_multimodal_cost(prompt, images, audio)`.
- Promotional credit experiment: two-week doubled credits for teams using both embeddings and multimodal generation in their first 90 days.

Roadmap & launch plan (quarterly milestones)

- Q2 2028: Internal alpha — runtime prototype, Node/Python SDKs, small-lab experiments 
- Q3 2028: External beta with 10 pilot customers (hosted only), pricing experiments, and telemetry validation
- Q4 2028: GA for hosted API and SDKs; initial Dedicated offering with warm capacity add-ons
- Q1 2029: Private (VPC) GA with on-prem preprocessors and enterprise retention controls

Dependencies and risks

- Dependencies: image/audio encoder licensing, containerized preprocessor packaging, console telemetry upgrades (event schema), and billing metering pipeline changes.
- Key risks: telemetry overcharges due to miscounted CUs, latency regressions for mixed workloads, and increased storage costs from image retention. Mitigations: conservative default TTLs, staged pricing experiments, and early-stage synthetic load tests.

Rollout checklist (release playbook)

1. Pre-launch (owner: product)
   - Complete runtime stress tests and perf benchmarks vs text baseline (SRE).
   - Finalize CU mapping and publish cost estimator tests (finance + billing).
   - Prepare SDKs and sample apps (devx).
   - Legal review for third-party encoders and customer data processing (legal/security).
2. Beta (owner: solutions + customer success)
   - Onboard pilot customers with telemetry dashboards and cost alerts.
   - Run two pricing experiments (fixed vs usage-based) and collect conversion metrics.
   - Document known limitations and add to support KB.
3. GA (owner: go-to-market + product)
   - Publish docs, migration guides, and console UX for multimodal telemetry.
   - Enable billing hooks and labeling for enterprise contracts.
   - Host launch webinar and create reference integration.
4. Post-GA (owner: eng-platform + optimize)
   - Monitor KPIs weekly and run cost-fidelity experiments.
   - Iterate on suggested quantization profiles for image encoders.

Telemetry & observability (minimum events and dashboards)

- Required events: multimodal.request.* (start, complete, fail), multimodal.cost.charge, multimodal.encoding.latency, multimodal.fallback.triggered.
- Dashboards: per-model P50/P95 latency by modality, CU consumption by tenant, top 10 routes by cost, fallback rate heatmap.

Launch notes / release summary (stub for release-notes)

- Release version: multimodal-runtime v1.0 (hosted)
- Highlights: Unified multimodal API, streaming responses with modality-aware chunks, SDK support for Node/Python/Go, initial pricing tiers and trial credits.
- Breaking changes: none for existing text-only endpoints.

Appendix: sample request and response (JSON simplified)

Sample request:
{ "model": "redwood-multi-1", "inputs": [ {"type": "text", "text": "Summarize the diagram and call out potential hazards."}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://example.com/diagram.png"} ], "fidelity": "balanced", "fallback_policy": "degrade_to_text" }

Sample streaming event (SSE chunk):
{ "event": "generation", "modality": "image", "delta_tokens": 24, "text": "The circuit shows...", "cost_delta_cu": 0.004 }
